chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abu al-Mu'za, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a free man, a slave, and a polytheist all have intercourse with a woman during the same period of purity, and they all claim the child, a lot is cast among them, and the child belongs to the one whose lot is drawn.
ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined when a free man, a slave, and a polytheist all claim a child from the same mother?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the application of *qur'ah* (casting lots) as a decisive legal mechanism when multiple claimants present equal evidentiary weight, specifically highlighting the inclusion of a polytheist (*mushrik*) alongside free and slave men. In Shia jurisprudence, this scenario underscores that social hierarchy or religious status does not inherently override the probabilistic nature of *qur'ah* when claims are mutually exclusive yet equally plausible. The attribution of the child to the winner serves to establish lineage (*nasab*) and associated rights, such as inheritance and maintenance, in the absence of superior proof.
